title: Buffon's Noodle Theorem: Expected Crossings for Curved Needles
description: Formalizes Buffon's Noodle Theorem (Barbier 1860): for a curve of length L dropped randomly on a floor with parallel lines spaced distance d apart, E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) regardless of the curve's shape. The key insight is linearity of expectation. Includes connection to the Cauchy-Crofton formula. 1 axiom for the probabilistic integral. 19 theorems.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom for integral probability of needle crossing a line.

overview.historicalContext: Buffon (1777) posed the needle problem; Barbier (1860) extended to curved needles using linearity of expectation.
overview.problemStatement: Prove Buffon's Noodle formula via linearity of expectation and segment-wise Buffon needle.
overview.proofStrategy: Decompose noodle into segments; apply E[crossings_i] = 2Lᵢ/(πd); sum via linearity of expectation.
keyInsights: **buffon_noodle_theorem**: Expected number of crossings depends only on total arc length, not curve shape
**Assumptions**: 1 axiom for integral probability of needle crossing a line.
